issues.legal_issue: Delivery of possession of immovable property without an effective conveyance does not constitute a transfer for capital-gains purposes.
material_facts: The seller agreed to sell the factory and its assets, and possession of the land, buildings, and machinery was given to the company during the relevant accounting year.
The company adopted the agreement only after that year, and the registered sale deed for the land was executed later.
No conveyance of the immovable assets was executed and registered during the relevant accounting year.
issues.conclusion: The land, buildings, machinery, and electrical fittings were not sold or transferred during the relevant accounting year, so no capital gains on those assets arose in that year.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, capital gains arise in the previous year in which a sale, exchange, or transfer of a capital asset takes place. For immovable property, title must pass by an effective conveyance; delivery of possession alone is not equivalent to conveyance. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax v. Bhurangya Coal Co., 34 I.T.R. 802, and rejected the contention based on section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act that possession alone effected the transfer.

predicates.immovable_asset: The asset at issue is immovable property or an asset for which title requires an effective conveyance.
predicates.possession_delivered: The transferor delivered possession of the asset to the proposed transferee.

predicates.immovable_asset_not_transferred_in_taxab: The immovable asset was not transferred during the taxable period for capital-gains purposes.

issues.definition: When a capital-gains assessment concerns immovable property, delivery of possession without an effective conveyance completed in the taxable period results in the asset being treated as not transferred in that period.

issues.legal_issue: Accounting entries do not determine when a sale or transfer of a capital asset takes place for capital-gains purposes.
material_facts: The company credited the seller with the agreed price and made corresponding asset-account entries during the relevant accounting year.
The seller also made corresponding entries in his own books during that year.
The legal conveyance of the immovable assets occurred only after the relevant accounting year.
issues.conclusion: The accounting entries were irrelevant to determining the date of sale or transfer under section 12B.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, deems capital gains to be income of the previous year in which the sale, exchange, or transfer took place. The date is determined by when the sale or transfer legally takes place, not by entries in account books.

issues.definition: When the date of a capital-asset transfer is disputed, entries recorded before the effective transfer do not determine the transfer date.

issues.legal_issue: Delivery of movable property transfers title when the delivery is made with the intention of passing title.
material_facts: The furniture was a movable asset included in the business sale.
Possession of the furniture was delivered to the company during the relevant accounting year.
The Court found that the delivery was made with the intention of passing title.
issues.conclusion: The furniture was transferred during the relevant accounting year, and any capital gain on its transfer accrued in that year.
issues.legal_principle: For movable property, title can pass by delivery when the delivery is made with the intention of passing title. Under section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, capital gains are attributed to the previous year in which the transfer takes place.

predicates.movable_asset_transferred_in_taxable_per: The movable asset was transferred during the taxable period.

issues.definition: When movable property is delivered during the taxable period with the intention of passing title, it is treated as transferred in that period.

issues.legal_issue: Goodwill is ordinarily transferred along with the transfer of the whole business, rather than by delivery of possession alone.
material_facts: Goodwill was included among the assets covered by the agreement to sell the business.
The agreement was adopted by the company after the relevant accounting year.
The Court found that the goodwill had not been transferred before the end of that year.
issues.conclusion: Goodwill was not transferred during the relevant accounting year, so no capital gain on it arose in that year.
issues.legal_principle: Goodwill is an intangible asset that ordinarily passes along with the transfer of the whole business. Under section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, capital gains are assessable in the previous year in which the asset is transferred.

predicates.whole_business_transfer_not_completed_in: The transfer of the whole business was not completed during the taxable period.
predicates.goodwill_not_transferred_in_taxable_peri: The goodwill was not transferred during the taxable period.

issues.definition: When goodwill is associated with a business and the whole business is not transferred during the taxable period, the goodwill is treated as not transferred in that period.

issues.legal_issue: Stock-in-trade is not a capital asset for purposes of the capital-gains charge under the applicable definition.
material_facts: Stocks were included among the assets covered by the business-sale agreement.
The stocks were held for the purposes of the seller's business.
issues.conclusion: The stocks were excluded from the definition of capital asset, and no capital gain on their sale or transfer accrued under section 12B.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12B of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, applies to gains from a capital asset. The Act's definition of capital asset excludes stock-in-trade held for the purposes of the assessee's business, profession, or vocation.
